newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Berlin opera member signs hotel bill Adolf Hitler.
newsitem.headline: Berlin opera member signs hotel bill Adolf Hitler.

text.p: The Berlin Opera now performing in Israel sacked one of its horn players on Saturday for signing a hotel bill "Adolf Hitler", the director of Israel's opera said.
"He thought he was making a joke and now he begins to realise what he has done and he will go with the next plane back to Germany," the director of the Berlin Opera told Israel radio.
The director of Israel's Opera, Hana Munitz, said the horn player had been fired and was being "expelled" from Israel.
"It caused us great trauma. I asked the director of the (Berlin) opera to my office this afternoon and informed him that I don't want this performer on the stage," said Munitz.
Several people, including Holocaust survivors, protested at the Tel Aviv opera house on Saturday night when the Berlin Opera was performing.

"I felt embarrassed, angry. What are you able to feel when you hear something like this even after 50 years people will not learn, they'll never learn, this hate will never pass" said one of the demonstrators.
A letter of apology was read at the start of a performance in Tel Aviv on Saturday night. The German Embassy in Israel also issued a statement expressing its regret over the incident.
